ShortDescription.Value: Emergency corridors, accidents that don't delete your traffic, and real towing.

Publish.LongDescription:
🚨 In vanilla, an ambulance queues at a red light like everybody else — and the traffic jammed behind a crash simply **evaporates**. This mod fixes the whole chain: getting there, the accident itself, and the clean-up afterwards.
## 🚑 Emergency corridor Cars ahead of a vehicle running with lights and siren pull to the side of their lane and a corridor opens up — a real *Rettungsgasse*. If that is not enough, the responder escalates step by step:
- ✅ Two-sided corridor along its whole route (configurable distance, default 120 m) - ✅ Traffic lights ahead switch green, so the queue can clear the crossing - ✅ Cars evade onto the shoulder when the responder is really stuck - ✅ Overtaking on a free parallel lane - ✅ Passing on the oncoming carriageway when there is a safe gap — and merging back in - ✅ Careful squeezing past cars that are boxed in themselves - ✅ **Pedestrians wait at the kerb** instead of strolling onto the crossing in front of the ambulance (vanilla only ever stops them at a red light) - ✅ Arrives and **stops at the scene** instead of circling the block forever
## 💥 Accidents that behave - ✅ **Traffic behind a crash waits instead of despawning.** This is the big one: on a fully blocked road vanilla finds no route past the wreck and quietly deletes the entire queue. - ✅ Cars approaching a wreck brake in time instead of piling into it - ✅ Settled wrecks are consolidated onto the outermost lane, so at least one lane stays passable — traffic squeezes past instead of dissolving
## 🚛 Real vehicle recovery - ✅ **Tow depot** — a new building that only recovers crashed vehicles, so its trucks go straight to the accident - ✅ **Tow truck** — a dedicated vehicle that actually **hauls the wreck away** instead of "repairing" it into thin air - ✅ The nearest capable van gets the job — or a tow truck from your depot if none is close - ✅ Recovery vehicles drive **directly** to the crash instead of finishing their road-repair round first - ✅ Amber beacons while responding, on scene and while towing - ✅ Traffic makes way for them too: stuck for 30 seconds they get a corridor and a green-light request, after a minute the same rights as an ambulance
## ⚙️ Compatibility & safety - **No Harmony patches, no replaced game systems.** The mod writes vanilla component fields from its own small systems; towing adds two tiny marker tags that are safe to remove with the mod. - **Save games stay compatible** — adding or removing the mod at any time is tested. (After uninstalling, leftover tow-depot buildings simply lose their model and can be bulldozed.) - Works with right-hand and left-hand traffic cities. - Every feature has its own toggle in the settings, so you can run just the parts you want. - English and German localization.
## 🔧 Options Every step of the chain can be switched off individually: corridor distance, squeezing, clearing undecided lanes, parallel-lane overtaking, green lights, oncoming lane, recovery priority, accident despawn protection, wreck consolidation, tow depot, towing, dedicated tow truck.
## 💬 Feedback Found a case where a responder gets stuck, or traffic behaves oddly around an accident? Please report it — with a screenshot if you can. There is a verbose logging option that writes diagnostics to `Logs/ClearTheWay.log`; that log makes bug reports much easier to act on.
Form without login: https://forms.gle/C2Yg6GXH6cZwAcdW9
Form with login (to attach screenshots): https://forms.gle/Q6gyAGZtrC9qXg4AA

Publish.ChangeLog:
This release is about tow trucks that actually drive home, and a main pass that costs noticeably less.
**Tow trucks no longer stand still after hooking a wreck** A loaded tow truck often stood still right after hooking its wreck, with the road ahead apparently free, and after about ten seconds the wreck went back up for recovery and the truck was removed. 0.1.13 blamed that on "no route to its own depot". The real reason was something else, and it was the normal case, not a rare one: - An accident is almost always two cars. The truck arrives from behind, hooks the rear one, and the front one still stands on its lane. The game plans a returning vehicle's route around blocked lanes, and on a road where a car cannot turn there was simply no way home. - The truck now gets a route that leads past the second wreck. Once it has stopped behind it, it pulls out beside it (away from the wreck, or toward the centre line when the wreck stands dead ahead), passes it and moves back into its lane once the wreck is behind it. - After a wreck has been towed away, the spot it stood on is released for the rest of the traffic. The game kept treating that lane as blocked until something else updated it, so cars kept routing around a wreck that was no longer there.
In a 27-minute test session every hooked wreck was delivered, and not a single truck was removed.
**A cheaper main pass** Every component read in the mod was rebuilt around one cached lookup per component type, instead of the game's general-purpose access with a safety check on every single read. Measured on a city of about 570,000 against 0.1.13, at comparable load: - With up to five emergency vehicles on duty the main pass costs 18 to 42 percent less per simulation step. - Pulling cars aside costs half as much per car; the second pass before car movement a quarter to a half less per step. - With many vehicles on duty the cost stays flat while the mod does up to half again as much work.
**Performance measurement for your own city** A new Performance tab in the mod options times each part of the mod and writes the results to Logs/ClearTheWay.log every few seconds. "All on" / "All off" switch everything; "Show single passes" opens one switch per part, including how long the mod waits for the game's own calculations. Everything is off by default and costs nothing while off. Changes take effect immediately, without a restart.
**Fixes** - An error message when the camera followed a tow truck the mod was removing. - Numbers in Logs/ClearTheWay.log are always written with a decimal point now, whatever language the game runs in.
**Worth reporting** A log with "Verbose logging" switched on, plus roughly where it happened: - A tow truck that stands still for a long time with a wreck on its hook, or one that is removed. - A tow truck driving along with a sideways offset away from any wreck. - Short regular stutters: please note the time, so they can be matched against the log.
